why: The only event claiming the statement is OpenAI's surface manuscript (recorded twice, as openai-039-seshadri and openai-math-039, both from 6 Oct 2026). I scored it whole: the statement's 'sufficiently large r' with unqualified points and d/sqrt(r) is the Wikipedia rendering of the conjecture the literature states at very general points with value sqrt(L^2/r), and the manuscript proves exactly that form for every smooth complex projective surface and ample L. It is unreviewed: the Lean build is not digestion and no human engaged. It is doubtful rather than not_credible, because its sibling manuscripts were withdrawn but no error is identified in this one. AI role is generated: the README credits the manuscripts to the model and names no human author. The plane manuscript is a case (one surface, one bundle). The higher-dimensional paper treats n>=3 only and the positive-characteristic paper treats a different field, so both are variants. Of the human in-window work: Laface-Ugaglia and Malara et al. are single or family instances; HJSS 2024 is conditional; Dionne-Roth's unconditional results are exact values for outer bundles on P1xP1 with no large-r Nagata-Biran equality, so it scores none. Before the snapshot, Nagata 1959 and the primer's theorem settle restricted r-sets (case), Hanumanthu 2016 is an asymptotic bound, and Ran is withdrawn.
doubts: Scope 'whole' for the OpenAI surface claim depends on reading the statement's unqualified points as very general and d/sqrt(r) as sqrt(L^2/r). Under a literal 'all configurations' reading it would only be a case. The two OpenAI surface rows describe one event. The record also conflicts on the higher-dimensional paper: openai-039-higher-dimensions says it includes n=2, while openai-math-039 says it treats only n>=3. I followed the later, fuller reading. The primer's Theorem 6.1.10 was read only through a summarising tool.
